rows.evidence: Q1: Material and Methods / Results - the authors report their own online questionnaire sent to 457 coffee growers in Bahia in 2021, with 34 responses analysed by relative and absolute frequencies.
rows.notes: The study is a perception survey of coffee growers about precision agriculture (PA) prospects, knowledge, adoption and obstacles. It reports no measurement of soil health or soil management outcomes and no own evidence on remote sensing. The only soil-related own result is that 62.1% of respondents thought PA is most important for soil management (a stated opinion, not an effect). The statements in the Discussion about geostatistics, sampling grids, P2O5/K2O dosage, chlorophyll index and soil compaction are results cited from other studies (Ferraz et al., Silva et al., Figueiredo et al., Zanella et al., Jorge et al.) and do not count. Remote sensing is not addressed at all as a technology in the study's own data.

notes: Full text appears complete. Study is a small (n=34) farmer questionnaire on PA perspectives in Bahia coffee growing; it provides no own evidence on remote sensing or soil management effects.
